history: Introduced in 1953 as Rolex's first divers' wristwatch, the Submariner was waterproof to 100 m at launch and set the template for the modern dive watch.
fun_fact: Sean Connery wore a Submariner (ref. 6538) as James Bond in Dr. No (1962).

history: Launched in 1955 for airline pilots, including those of Pan Am, the GMT-Master tracked a second time zone with a 24-hour hand and two-tone bezel.
fun_fact: The red-and-blue bezel became known as "Pepsi"; the blue-and-black version introduced in 2013 is nicknamed "Batman".

history: Launched in 1963 and named for Daytona Beach racing, the Cosmograph is Rolex's chronograph with a tachymeter bezel for measuring average speed.
Launched in 1945 for Rolex's 40th anniversary, the Datejust was the first self-winding chronometer wristwatch to show the date in a window at 3 o'clock.
highlights: Cyclops magnifying lens over the date
fun_fact: The Jubilee bracelet was designed specifically for the Datejust's 1945 debut.

history: Launched in 1953 following Hillary and Norgay's first ascent of Everest, the Explorer is Rolex's purist three-hand tool watch with its 3-6-9 dial.
The Oyster Perpetual descends from the 1926 Oyster, marketed as the first waterproof wristwatch case, and the 1931 Perpetual rotor.
fun_fact: Rolex sponsored swimmer Mercedes Gleitze, the first British woman to swim the English Channel, as one of its early ambassadors.

history: Launched in 1957 and qualified by NASA for all manned missions in 1965, the Speedmaster was worn on the Moon during Apollo 11 in 1969.
fun_fact: During Apollo 13, Jack Swigert used his Speedmaster to time a critical 14-second engine burn for the return to Earth.

history: Launched in 1993, the Diver 300M became famous as James Bond's watch from GoldenEye (1995) onward.
fun_fact: Pierce Brosnan wore a Seamaster Diver 300M as Bond in GoldenEye (1995), starting Omega's run as 007's watch.

history: The Aqua Terra arrived in 2002 as the dressier, everyday member of the Seamaster family.

us_retail_price: Discontinued ref.; current Planet Ocean models $8,600–$9,200 on Omega US
history: The Planet Ocean joined the Seamaster line in 2005 as Omega's heavier-duty professional dive watch.
The Black Bay debuted in 2012, drawing on Tudor's 1950s Submariner-era divers and kick-starting the brand's revival.
fun_fact: Montres Tudor SA has made Tudor watches since 6 March 1946. Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf conceived Tudor so authorized Rolex dealers could sell a watch with Rolex-like reliability at a lower price.

movement: Calibre MT5400-U, automatic (COSC + METAS Master Chronometer); previous M79030N: MT5402
history: Released in 2018, the Black Bay 58 is named for 1958, the year of Tudor's first 200 m dive watch, the 'Big Crown' ref. 7924.
fun_fact: The '58' refers to 1958, the year of Tudor's ref. 7924 'Big Crown' diver.

history: Launched in 2022, the Black Bay Pro is a 39 mm fixed-bezel GMT drawing on Tudor's 1950s professional-watch heritage.
The Pelagos line launched in 2012 as Tudor's technical titanium diver; the smaller Pelagos 39 followed in 2022.

The Snowflake first appeared in 2005; when Grand Seiko became a standalone brand in 2017 it was reissued as the SBGA211, with a dial evoking wind-carved snow on the Hotaka mountains seen from the Shinshu Watch Studio.
Seiko's Laurel Alpinist launched in 1959 for Japan's mountaineering boom.
The cushion-cased 'Turtle' revives Seiko's 1976 6309 diver, a favourite of divers and collectors.
Louis Cartier created the Santos in 1904 for aviator Alberto Santos-Dumont, who needed to read the time in flight.
highlights: Square case with exposed screws on the bezel
fun_fact: It is often described as the first pilot's watch.

us_retail_price: $4,400 (CRWSTA0106, large, steel bracelet, Cartier US); WSTA0041 no longer listed
history: The Tank prototype of 1917 was inspired by the Renault tanks of the First World War; it entered production in 1919.
fun_fact: The design dates to 1917, but it went on sale in 1919.

history: Designed by Gérald Genta and launched in 1972, the Royal Oak is the archetypal luxury steel sports watch with an integrated bracelet.
Gérald Genta's 1976 Nautilus, with its ship's-porthole-inspired case, became one of the most sought-after luxury sports watches.
Introduced in 1997 as a younger, sportier relative of the Nautilus.
Launched in 1952 for the AOPA, the Navitimer put a circular slide rule on the bezel for pilots' flight calculations.
The Superocean Heritage revives Breitling's 1957 Superocean dive watch.
Jack Heuer launched the Carrera in 1963, named after the Carrera Panamericana road race.
fun_fact: The race was the Carrera Panamericana, a 1950s Mexican road race.

history: Launched in 1969 with the Calibre 11, the Monaco was the first water-resistant square-cased automatic chronograph.
fun_fact: Steve McQueen wore a Monaco in the 1971 film Le Mans.

history: The Portugieser line began when Portuguese merchants asked IWC for a wristwatch with marine-chronometer accuracy, achieved with a large pocket-watch movement.
Launched in 2021, the Chronomaster Sport uses the El Primero, introduced in 1969 as one of the first automatic chronographs.
fun_fact: Zenith employee Charles Vermot secretly kept El Primero tooling and plans after production stopped in 1975, enabling its 1984 revival.

history: Created in 1931 for British polo players in India whose watch crystals kept breaking, the Reverso's case flips over to protect the dial.
fun_fact: The name comes from the Latin for 'I turn around'.

history: Panerai supplied instruments to the Italian Navy; the Luminor takes its name from its luminous material, and its 1949 design introduced the crown-protecting bridge.
fun_fact: Sylvester Stallone wore a Luminor in the 1996 film Daylight.

history: The PRX revives a 1978 Tissot integrated-bracelet design; the automatic Powermatic 80 version arrived in 2021.
fun_fact: PRX stands for Precise and Robust; the X refers to 10 bar water resistance.

history: The Khaki Field Mechanical recreates Hamilton's field watches made to US military specification; Hamilton supplied watches to US forces in WWII and Vietnam.
fun_fact: Hamilton says the Khaki Field Mechanical 38 mm was featured in Sonic the Hedgehog (2020), worn by Sheriff Tom Wachowski, played by James Marsden.

history: Launched in 2022, the Spirit Zulu Time adds a GMT function to Longines' pilot-inspired Spirit line.
highlights: True GMT with jumping local hour
fun_fact: 'Zulu' is aviation shorthand for UTC; Longines first used the Zulu Time name in 1925.

history: Oris introduced its in-house Calibre 400 in 2020 and fitted it to the Aquis diver.
Introduced in 1967 for professional saturation divers, the Sea-Dweller added a helium escape valve.
Breitling's modern Chronomat launched in 1984; the 2020 redesign restored the Rouleaux bracelet.
Launched in 2007, the Ballon Bleu is known for its rounded case and the blue cabochon crown set in a protective arc.
Introduced in 1996, the Overseas is Vacheron Constantin's luxury sports line, with a bezel inspired by the Maltese cross.
fun_fact: Vacheron Constantin, founded in 1755, claims the longest uninterrupted watchmaking history.

history: Cocktail Time began in 2010 as a collaboration with Tokyo bartender Shinobu Ishigaki of Bar Ishinohana, whose cocktails inspired the sunburst dials.
The Mark XX continues IWC's line of Mark pilot's watches, with a clean cockpit-instrument dial and an automatic movement with a five-day power reserve.
Omega was founded by Louis Brandt in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, in 1848 and took the Omega name in 1903.
Omega introduced the Speedmaster in 1957 as a sport and racing chronograph, the same year it launched the Railmaster and the Seamaster 300.
The Speedmaster Automatic, informally called the Speedmaster Reduced, was introduced in 1988 as a smaller, cheaper version of the Speedmaster.
The Seamaster line dates to 1948. In 1957 Omega added the Seamaster 300, a watch designed for professional divers.
highlights: Unidirectional bezel with black ceramic ring

model: Speedmaster Dark Side of the Moon
history: Omega introduced the Dark Side of the Moon sub-collection in 2013, with a ceramic case and a zirconium-oxide ceramic dial.

The Ocean Star M026.430.11.041.00 (WatchMaxx lists it as Ocean Star 200) is a 42.5 mm, 11.75 mm thick diver with the Mido Calibre Powermatic 80 (ETA C07.621), 80-hour power reserve and 200 m water resistance, per Jomashop.
The Captain Cook R32505203 is a 42 mm, 12.1 mm thick steel diver with a blue dial, 80-hour power reserve and 200 m water resistance, per Jomashop.
Seiko was founded in Tokyo in 1881 by Kintarō Hattori; it launched Japan's first diver's wristwatch in 1965 and introduced the world's first commercial quartz wristwatch in 1969.
Citizen traces its origins to the Shokosha Watch Research Institute, founded in 1918, and began marketing its solar-charging technology under the Eco-Drive name in the mid-1990s.
The Aquascaphe Classic Blue checked here is a 39 mm steel diver with a Miyota Caliber 9039 and 200 m water resistance, per Jomashop.

Rolex introduced the Day-Date at the Swiss Industries Fair in Basel in 1956. It was the first watch to show both the date and the day of the week spelled in full. Lyndon B. Johnson became the first US president to wear a gold Day-Date.
The Yacht-Master was first introduced in 1992 as reference 16628 in 18-karat yellow gold.

Introduced in 1945, the Air-King was part of Rolex's post-war aviation-themed watches and is the only model from that series still in production. Rolex re-introduced it in 2018, with a dial inspired by the counter Rolex built for the Bloodhound SSC land-speed car.
Rolex introduced the Explorer II in 1971 with a fixed 24-hour bezel and an independent 24-hour hand to help cave explorers tell day from night.
Rolex introduced the Milgauss in 1956 (ref. 6541), brought it back in 2007 as ref. 116400 after nearly 20 years, and discontinued it in 2023.
The 1908 checked here, m52508-0006, is 18 kt yellow gold with a part-domed, part-fluted bezel, per Rolex.
